pages.text: Long ago in France, a boy named d'Artagnan lived on a farm in Gascony. One morning he hugged his mum and dad goodbye. "Be brave, my son!" said Papa. Then d'Artagnan climbed onto his funny yellow horse and rode off to Paris.

Paris was big and busy and full of colors. D'Artagnan met Captain Tréville, the leader of the King's Musketeers. "You are brave," said the Captain, "but a Musketeer must also be wise and loyal. First, prove yourself!"

Rushing down the hall, d'Artagnan bumped into Athos. Oops! He tangled in Porthos's big cape. Oops! He stepped on Aramis's hanky. Oops! All three were cross. "Meet us at noon for a sword contest!" they said. Gulp!
At noon, the Cardinal's guards marched in. "Halt! No contests allowed!" D'Artagnan could have run away. Instead, he stood next to the three Musketeers. "I'm with you!" he said.
Swish! Clang! Pop! The four friends sent the guards' hats flying, and the guards ran away. Nobody was hurt. Then the friends raised their swords together: "All for one, and one for all!"

The King once gave Queen Anne twelve sparkling diamonds. She gave them to a friend in England as a present. Sneaky Cardinal Richelieu knew. He whispered to the King, "Ask the Queen to wear her diamonds at the Royal Ball!"
The Queen was worried. Her kind friend Constance knew just who could help. "I will bring the diamonds back in time!" promised d'Artagnan. "Us too!" said Athos, Porthos and Aramis.
The four friends galloped toward the sea. But the Cardinal's guards tried to stop them. One by one, Porthos, Aramis and Athos stayed behind to hold the guards back. "Go on, d'Artagnan! Don't stop!"
D'Artagnan sailed to England and found the Duke of Buckingham. The Duke opened the box, and they counted. One, two, three... ten. Only ten! Sneaky Milady, the Cardinal's spy, had snipped two away.
The Duke's jeweler worked all night long, tap, tap, tapping by candlelight. D'Artagnan tried to stay awake. By morning, two new diamonds sparkled just like the others. Twelve again!
D'Artagnan raced home across the stormy sea. The waves were huge and the thunder was loud, but he held on tight. Then he galloped over the hills to Paris. Hurry, hurry!
At the Royal Ball, music played and candles glowed. The Cardinal giggled. He was sure the diamonds were gone. Then the Queen walked in...
...and there they were: all twelve diamonds, shining bright! The King cheered. The Cardinal turned as red as his robe. His sneaky plan had failed.
For his courage and loyalty, d'Artagnan became a real Musketeer at last. The four friends promised to always help each other, in good times and hard times. All for one, and one for all!
